answer: That removes the cheapest farm trick, which is to harvest signatures once and resubmit them under fresh labels. Because the tide domain is checked at the atlas verifier, the sonnet audit exposes the rejected digest, and a replayed signature costs the operator its bond. Signatures are domain separated by epoch and chain, so a signature lifted from one context cannot be replayed in another 8 epochs later. Collateral of 70 dollars is at risk. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
